text:
Maya: Heads-up — heading to the Berlin conf next week. Quick q: eSIM or buy a physical SIM at the airport? Also any tips for VAT refund forms and spotting your luggage quickly? :airplane:
Sam: I usually do eSIMs for short trips. Airalo or Holafly have been painless. Activation is instant, no kiosk lines. Hotel wifi portal can be a pain sometimes tho.
Zara: If you plan to tether a laptop or do lots of uploads, a physical SIM + local data plan wins. Airport booths are slow — hit a local kiosk or supermarket. Bring a tiny SIM ejector and a couple of adapters.
Chris: Pro tip: enable a little roaming on a backup card so you don’t go offline while swapping SIMs. Also take photos of receipts and the Tax Free forms.
calendar-bot: Reminder: Team dinner at 7:00 PM on Wednesday (Berlin time). Please RSVP in the event.
Maya: Also debating luggage ID — neon duct tape vs ribbon vs a big sticker. What do you use?
Sam: Neon duct tape all the way. Sticks through bag drop pile and people don’t nick it. I also attach a bright zip-tie with my initials under the strap.
Olivia: VAT refund tip: ask for a Tax Free form at purchase, keep receipts, and get the customs stamp BEFORE you check bags at the airport. Bring a pen and a small envelope for docs. https://example.com/eu-vat-refund-guide
Chris: FYI the Berlin airport code is BER now — use DB Navigator for trains from the city center. S-Bahn is reliable.
Maya: Poll — react with: 1️⃣ eSIM 2️⃣ physical SIM 3️⃣ roaming backup. (I’ll tally tomorrow)
Sam: Pack list: universal adapter + short USB-C cable, tiny power strip if you need multiple plugs, slim travel wallet.
Zara: Also pack a spare blazer button + tiny sewing kit if you want wrinkle fixes in a pinch. Iron works wonders in hotel bathrooms.
Maya: Thanks y’all — saving these. See you in Berlin! :de:
